deep.reconstruction:
Topic (heading 'Verbreitung der Wärme im Ellipsoid', dated Easter/Whitsun 1856): separating the heat equation u_t = a^2 Δu in confocal ellipsoidal coordinates, then a large-parameter (WKB / Liouville–Green) expansion of the separated ordinary differential equation.

(1) Confocal coordinates. Put f(s) = x^2/(s+α) + y^2/(s+β) + z^2/(s+γ) − 1, and Θ(s) = (s+α)(s+β)(s+γ). The three roots λ, μ, ν of f = 0 are the ellipsoidal coordinates. Then f(s) = −(s−λ)(s−μ)(s−ν)/Θ(s), hence −f'(λ) = (λ−μ)(λ−ν)/Θ(λ). The boxed sign table counts roots by following the sign changes of f(s) between its poles and at ±∞ (f → −1). This shows one root in each interval.

(2) Gradient of λ. Implicit differentiation of f(λ; x, y, z) = 0 gives 2x/(λ+α) + f'(λ) ∂λ/∂x = 0. Squaring and summing, and using Σ x^2/(λ+α)^2 = −f'(λ) (my step), gives |∇λ|^2 f'(λ)^2 = −4 f'(λ). That is, |∇λ|^2 = −4/f'(λ) = 4Θ(λ)/((λ−μ)(λ−ν)). The same holds cyclically for μ and ν. The coordinates are orthogonal, so the Lamé scale factor is h_λ = ½√(−f'(λ)).

(3) Volume element. dx dy dz = (1/8) √(−f'(λ) f'(μ) f'(ν)) dλ dμ dν. Riemann computes −f'(λ) f'(μ) f'(ν) = (λ−μ)^2 (λ−ν)^2 (μ−ν)^2 / (−Θ(λ)Θ(μ)Θ(ν)).

(4) Dirichlet integral. |∇u|^2 dV = (1/8) dλ dμ dν √(...) · Σ(−4 u_λ^2 / f'(λ)). This equals (½) dλ dμ dν / √(−Θ(λ)Θ(μ)Θ(ν)) · [(μ−ν) Θ(λ) u_λ^2 + (ν−λ) Θ(μ) u_μ^2 + (λ−μ) Θ(ν) u_ν^2].

(5) Laplacian. Varying the Dirichlet integral (equivalently, using the formula (1/J) Σ ∂(J g^{ii} ∂_i u)) gives
Δu · (λ−μ)(λ−ν)(μ−ν) = 4[(μ−ν) √Θ(λ) ∂_λ(√Θ(λ) u_λ) + (ν−λ) √Θ(μ) ∂_μ(√Θ(μ) u_μ) + (λ−μ) √Θ(ν) ∂_ν(√Θ(ν) u_ν)].
The heat equation therefore becomes D u_t = 4a^2 [...], with D = (λ−μ)(λ−ν)(μ−ν).

(6) Separation. Take u = U(λ) M(μ) N(ν) e^{−4a^2 g^2 t}. Implicitly Riemann uses the identities Σ(μ−ν) = 0, Σ(μ−ν)λ = 0 and Σ(μ−ν)λ^2 = D. The marginal note '−4gg aa u λλ' and the remark ∂u_λ/∂t = ∂u_μ/∂t = ∂u_ν/∂t refer to this. Each factor then satisfies the same equation
Θ(λ) U'' + ½ Θ'(λ) U' + (g^2 λ^2 + hλ + k) U = 0, with g^2 > 0.
This is the ellipsoidal wave equation: Lamé's equation with an extra g^2 λ^2 term. Two earlier sketch lines (constant 'αλ+β', the factor aa without 4, and a sign) are rough drafts of this step.

(7) Normal form. With the uniformizing variable e = ∫ dλ/√Θ(λ), so that d/de = √Θ d/dλ, the equation becomes U_ee + g^2 ψ(λ) U = 0. Here ψ = (λ−η)(λ−ε), writing g^2 λ^2 + hλ + k = g^2 (λ−η)(λ−ε). Riemann notes the location of the separation constants η and ε relative to the singular points (δ > η > β, γ > ε > α, with δ apparently an extra bounding parameter). This is an oscillation/eigenvalue-location remark.

(8) Asymptotics in g. Put w = exp ∫ v de, giving the Riccati equation v^2 + v_e + g^2 ψ = 0. Use the ansatz v = i(g a + a_0 + Σ_{n≥1} a_n g^{−n}). Comparing powers of g:
- order g^2: a = √ψ;
- order g: −2a a_0 + i a_e = 0, so a_0 = (i/2) d log a/de;
- general: −Σ_{ν=0}^{n} a_ν a_{n−ν} − 2a a_{n+1} + i a_n' = 0.
This gives a_1 = (i/2) a^{−1/2} d(a^{−1/2} a_0)/de and a_2 = (i/2) d(a^{−1} a_1)/de. It also gives a_3 = (i/2) a_2'/a − a_1^2/(2a) − a_0 a_2/a.

(9) Integrated phase. ∫ v de = i g ∫ √(ψ/Θ) dλ − ¼ log ψ + g^{−1}-term. The g^{−1} term is (i/g)∫ a_1 de = (i/(2g)) ∫ φ φ_ee de with φ = ψ^{−1/4}. Integrating by parts and returning to λ gives the boundary term −(i/(8g)) ψ^{−3/2} ψ' √Θ plus an integral term ∝ (1/g) ∫ ψ^{−5/2} √Θ ψ'^2 dλ. Riemann's leading behaviour remark is log w ≈ −g√(−λ) as λ → ∞. Overall this is the Liouville–Green/WKB expansion of the separated equation, presumably to get asymptotics of high modes.
errors: Recurring notational slips (or transcription) f(λ) for f'(λ): in '2x/(λ+α)+f(λ)∂λ/∂x=0', 'f(λ)(...)=−4' and '−f(λ)=(λ−μ)(λ−ν)/Θ'. All must be f'(λ).
First draft of the Dirichlet integral omits the factor 4 (|∇λ|^2 = −4/f'). It is corrected in the second version.
Early sketch '... = 4(λ−μ)(μ−ν)(ν−λ) ∂u/∂t': (λ−μ)(μ−ν)(ν−λ) = −(λ−μ)(λ−ν)(μ−ν), so the sign differs from the later correct version. The aa/4aa factor is also inconsistent there.
The early line 'aa√Θ ∂(√Θ u_λ)/∂λ = 4λλ u_t + (αλ+β)u' reuses α, β as arbitrary constants. This clashes with the semi-axis parameters and is only a draft.
The sign table writes poles at s = +α, +β, +γ, whereas with denominators λ+α etc. the poles are at s = −α, −β, −γ. This is a sign convention slip, harmless for counting roots.

In the g^{−1} phase term the integration by parts gives (i/(2g))[φφ_e − ∫φ_e^2 de] with φ = ψ^{−1/4}. The integral term should therefore carry a minus sign: −(i/(32g)) ∫ ψ^{−5/2} √Θ ψ'^2 dλ. Riemann's boundary term −(i/(8g)) ψ^{−3/2} ψ' √Θ is correct, but the page as read shows '+' on the integral term. This is either a slip or an ambiguous reading. The intermediate prefactor 'i/(2g) ∫ a^{−1/2} d a^{−3/2} ∂a/∂e · i/2' also seems to drop a factor i/2 (the correct total prefactor is −i/(4g)).

results.what: Confocal ellipsoidal coordinates: −f'(λ) = (λ−μ)(λ−ν)/Θ(λ), |∇λ|^2 = −4/f'(λ), volume element and Dirichlet integral
Laplacian in ellipsoidal coordinates in the symmetric form D·Δu = 4Σ(μ−ν)√Θ(λ)∂_λ(√Θ(λ)∂_λ u)
Separation of the heat equation in an ellipsoid via Σ(μ−ν)λ^2 = D, giving ΘU'' + ½Θ'U' + (g^2λ^2 + hλ + k)U = 0
results.modern_name: Ellipsoidal wave equation (Lamé–Wangerin type, Helmholtz separation in ellipsoidal coordinates)
results.usually_credited_to: Niven (1880s, heat conduction in ellipsoids); later Möglich (1927), Arscott

results.what: Interlacing/location of the separation-constant roots η, ε relative to the singular points
results.usually_credited_to: Klein (1881), Bôcher (1890s) for systematic oscillation theorems

results.what: Formal large-parameter expansion via the Riccati equation v^2 + v' + g^2ψ = 0, with recursive coefficients a_{n+1} and compact forms a_1 = (i/2)a^{−1/2}(a^{−1/2}a_0)', a_2 = (i/2)(a^{−1}a_1)'
results.modern_name: WKB / Liouville–Green asymptotic expansion to higher order (Riccati recursion)
results.usually_credited_to: Carlini (1817), Liouville and Green (1837); higher-order recursion often associated with later authors (e.g. Dunham 1932 in physics)

results.what: First correction term of the phase in closed form: −¼ log ψ and (i/(2g))∫ψ^{−1/4}(ψ^{−1/4})_ee de, reduced to an integral of ψ^{−5/2}√Θψ'^2 plus a boundary term
results.modern_name: Liouville–Green error-control function / second-order WKB correction

deep.surprise_reason: The coordinate machinery is Lamé's and routine. Two things are less expected in 1856: setting up the time-dependent heat problem in an ellipsoid, which leads to the ellipsoidal wave equation usually associated with Niven's work in the 1880s, and a systematic all-orders Riccati/WKB expansion in the separation parameter. Riemann is known to have lectured on heat conduction and to have used asymptotic methods, and the expansion technique goes back to Carlini, Liouville and Green. So this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a priority-changing result.

transcription_corrections: In the a_1 line the middle expression should be (i/2)(1/a·∂a_0/∂e − ½ a_0 (∂a/∂e)/(aa)), not '+ i/2 a_0 …'; this is required for the final equality a_1 = (i/2)a^{−1/2}∂(a^{−1/2}a_0)/∂e.
The early line reading '(αλ+β)u' uses α, β as generic separation constants (later h, k), not the ellipsoid parameters.
The marginal fragment '−4gg aa u λλ' is the time-derivative term substituted from u ∝ e^{−4a^2g^2t}.
The sign of the integral term in the final g^{−1} correction is uncertain in the image ('+' or '−'); mathematically it should be '−'.
